beaches.name: Sandy Hook
beaches.area: Gateway National Recreation Area · Monmouth County
beaches.waveNote: Usually moderate in summer; rougher in storms
beaches.entryNote: Beach parking fee, charged 8 a.m.–6 p.m. from Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day. Season pass $100. Cashless: cards or contactless only. Free for military members and veterans with an America the Beautiful pass.
beaches.parking: Several large beach lots. On hot summer weekends they fill up and the park can close the entrance until spaces open, so arrive early.
beaches.description: A seven-mile barrier spit at the top of the Jersey Shore, with wide ocean beaches, dunes, the 1764 Sandy Hook Lighthouse and views of the New York skyline across the bay.
features: Restrooms & showers at the beach areas
beaches.safety: Swim only at guarded beaches and watch for rip currents. Some beaches are a long walk from the lot, so bring water and shade.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Asbury Park
beaches.waveNote: Small summer waves; bigger with fall swells
beaches.entryNote: $10 on weekends and holidays. Season badge $70 for adults, $20 for teens and seniors. Badges aren’t needed after Labor Day.
beaches.parking: Metered street parking and paid lots near the boardwalk, paid by app or kiosk. It fills up on summer weekends.
beaches.description: A lively mile-long boardwalk with the historic Convention Hall and Paramount Theatre, restaurants and bars right by the sand, and a designated surfing beach.
beaches.safety: Swim only between the lifeguard flags. Surfing is limited to the marked surfing beaches.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Point Pleasant Beach
beaches.entryNote: Jenkinson’s Beach: $15 on weekends and holidays, and kids under 12 get in free with an adult. Season badge $130 for adults. Buy daily admission at any open beach gate.
beaches.parking: Paid lots and metered street parking near the boardwalk. Lots fill early on summer weekends.
beaches.description: Home of Jenkinson’s Boardwalk, with rides, arcades, an aquarium, mini golf and boardwalk food right behind the sand.
beaches.safety: Swim at guarded beaches, and keep an eye on kids in the busy boardwalk crowds.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Seaside Heights
beaches.entryNote: Kids under 12 free. Weekly badge $50, season badge $75 ($15 for seniors).
beaches.parking: Metered streets and private lots. Lots fill on summer weekends.
beaches.description: A loud, bright boardwalk town with Casino Pier’s rides over the ocean, arcades and pizza stands, and a wide beach in front of it all.
beaches.safety: Swim at guarded beaches only. The boardwalk gets very crowded on summer nights.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Island Beach State Park
beaches.waveNote: Open ocean; rougher on windy days
beaches.lifeguardNote: At the ocean swimming areas in summer
beaches.entryNote: Summer weekend rate for New Jersey cars; out-of-state cars pay $20. Weekdays cost less, and the NJ State Parks annual pass ($50) also works. Rates vary by season, so check the park’s site.
beaches.parking: Lots along the park road. On hot summer weekends the park closes the gate once it’s full, so arrive early.
beaches.description: About ten miles of undeveloped barrier island, with dunes, maritime forest and almost no buildings. It’s one of the last natural stretches of the Jersey Shore.
features: Bring your own food and water
beaches.safety: Swim only at the guarded areas, and use the marked paths over the dunes.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Beach Haven
beaches.entryNote: Weekly badge $20, season badge $50 ($40 if bought before May 31).
beaches.parking: Mostly street parking in town. It gets tight near the beach on summer weekends.
beaches.description: A classic Long Beach Island town with wide guarded beaches, a small-town center of shops and ice cream, and the Fantasy Island amusement park a few blocks from the sand.
features: Shops, ice cream & food in town
beaches.safety: Swim at guarded beaches and watch for rip currents, especially after storms.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Atlantic City
beaches.lifeguardNote: Atlantic City Beach Patrol, summer daytime
beaches.entryNote: No beach badge needed.
beaches.parking: Casino garages and paid lots along the boardwalk, plus metered street parking.
beaches.description: Miles of free beach in front of America’s first boardwalk (1870), lined with casinos, Steel Pier rides, shops and food.
beaches.safety: Swim only at guarded beaches, between the lifeguard flags.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Ocean City
beaches.entryNote: Weekly badge $20, season badge $35 ($30 before June 1). Kids 11 and under are free.
beaches.parking: Metered streets and lots near the boardwalk. It fills up on summer weekends.
beaches.description: A dry town (no alcohol sales) with a 2.5-mile boardwalk of rides, mini golf, fudge and pizza, and wide guarded beaches.
beaches.safety: Swim at guarded beaches. Surfing is only allowed at the marked surfing beaches.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Wildwood
beaches.lifeguardNote: Guarded beaches about 10 a.m.–5:30 p.m. in summer
beaches.entryNote: No beach tags in Wildwood, North Wildwood or Wildwood Crest.
beaches.parking: Metered streets and private lots near the boardwalk.
beaches.description: One of the widest beaches on the East Coast, with a long walk to the water, Morey’s Piers rides and waterparks, and the boardwalk tram car.
beaches.safety: Swimming is only allowed at guarded beaches. The sand is wide and hot, so bring shoes.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Cape May
beaches.entryNote: Season badge $40.
beaches.parking: Metered street parking and lots near the beach. It fills up on summer weekends.
beaches.description: The southern tip of New Jersey, with Victorian streets, a beachfront promenade, dolphin-watching boat trips and Cape May Lighthouse nearby.
beaches.safety: Swim at guarded beaches and watch for rip currents near the jetties.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Siesta Key Beach
beaches.lifeguardNote: Four lifeguard stations; hours vary by season
beaches.entryNote: Public beach park.
beaches.parking: About 950 free spaces. They fill quickly in peak season (January–April), so arrive early or take the free trolley.
beaches.description: A wide beach of bright white, powder-soft quartz sand with gentle Gulf water, regularly named one of the best beaches in America.
beaches.safety: Swim near a lifeguard station and watch for rip current warnings on windy days.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Clearwater Beach
beaches.lifeguardNote: 10 a.m.–5 p.m. daily; towers staffed by season and weather
beaches.entryNote: Public beach.
beaches.parking: Paid city lots and garages near Pier 60. Rates vary by lot, so check the meter. Lots fill on weekends.
beaches.description: Wide, soft white sand on the Gulf, calm water and beachfront restaurants, with Pier 60 at the center for watching the sunset.
beaches.safety: Swim near a staffed lifeguard tower. Parts of Pier 60 may be closed after storm damage, so check before you go.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: South Beach
beaches.waveNote: Usually gentle; rougher with winter fronts
beaches.lifeguardNote: Miami Beach Ocean Rescue towers staffed daily; check posted hours
beaches.entryNote: Public beach.
beaches.parking: Paid garages and metered street parking. Rates rise on busy and event weekends, and spaces near the beach fill fast.
beaches.hours: Lummus Park is open sunrise to midnight.
beaches.description: Miami’s famous city beach: wide sand and blue-green water in front of the pastel Art Deco hotels of Ocean Drive.
features: Art Deco buildings along Ocean Drive
beaches.safety: Swim near a staffed lifeguard tower and check the warning flags before going in.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Bahia Honda State Park
beaches.lifeguardNote: No lifeguards; swim at your own risk
beaches.entryNote: For 2–8 people, plus a 50¢ per person Monroe County surcharge. Single-person vehicles $4.50; walk-ins and cyclists $2.50.
beaches.parking: Parking inside the park is included with entry. It can fill on busy days.
beaches.description: A Florida Keys state park with clear, shallow turquoise water, three beaches on the Atlantic and Florida Bay, and views of the old Bahia Honda Rail Bridge.
features: Views of the old Bahia Honda Rail Bridge
beaches.safety: There are no lifeguards. Stay away from the Bahia Honda Channel, where the currents are very strong.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Daytona Beach
beaches.lifeguardNote: Volusia County Beach Safety towers; staffing varies, check the Volusia Beaches app
beaches.entryNote: Free to walk on. Driving and parking on the sand need a pass, with different prices for residents and visitors; check Park Volusia for current rates.
beaches.parking: Drive-on beach sections (when the tide allows) and off-beach lots, both paid.
beaches.description: A wide, hard-packed beach where you can still drive and park on the sand in some sections, with the boardwalk and Main Street Pier at its center.
beaches.safety: Watch for cars on the drive-on sections and swim near a staffed lifeguard tower; rip currents are common.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Waikīkī Beach
beaches.waveNote: Gentle rollers; bigger south swells in summer
beaches.entryNote: Public beach, open to everyone.
beaches.parking: Scarce and metered. Use a hotel or shopping garage or the Fort DeRussy lot; most visitors walk from their hotel.
beaches.description: About two miles of golden sand in front of Diamond Head, with soft rolling waves where beginner surf lessons happen right off the sand. Busy, buzzy and in the heart of Honolulu.
features: Restrooms & showers at Kūhiō Beach Park
beaches.safety: The water is crowded. Watch for surfers and outrigger canoes in the lesson areas.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Hanauma Bay
beaches.waveNote: Sheltered by a reef inside an old volcanic crater
beaches.entryNote: For non-residents, plus an online fee. Free for Hawaiʻi residents, kids 12 and under, and active military. Non-residents need a reservation, released 2 days ahead at 7 a.m. HST.
beaches.parking: $3 for non-residents, $1 for residents. Cash only, first come first served, even with a reservation.
beaches.description: A protected nature preserve in a volcanic crater, with clear, calm water over coral reef. It’s Oʻahu’s best-known place to snorkel with reef fish and turtles.
beaches.safety: Don’t stand on the coral or touch turtles. Book your entry two days ahead.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Lanikai Beach
beaches.entryNote: Reached by public paths between homes.
beaches.parking: No lot, and street parking is very limited and strictly enforced. Park at Kailua Beach Park and walk.
beaches.description: A slim ribbon of powder-soft sand facing the twin Mokulua islets. It’s often called the most beautiful beach in Hawaiʻi, and it was No. 9 on Dr. Beach’s 2025 list of top US beaches.
beaches.safety: There are no lifeguards or facilities. Park legally and use the marked public paths.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Waimea Bay
beaches.waveNote: Glassy in summer; winter waves can top 20 ft
beaches.entryNote: Public beach park.
beaches.parking: Free lot. It fills very early on weekends and big-surf days.
beaches.description: A deep, sandy bay that’s calm enough to swim and snorkel in summer and home to giant surf in winter. The famous jump rock sits at the south end.
beaches.safety: Winter surf and currents are deadly. Swim roughly May–Sept, and only jump from the rock when it’s calm and the lifeguards say so.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Kailua Beach Park
beaches.entryNote: Public beach park.
beaches.parking: Big free lot.
beaches.description: Wide, soft sand and turquoise water on Kailua Bay, with an easy kayak launch toward the offshore islets and steady breezes for windsurfers and kiteboarders.
beaches.safety: Trade winds can push kayaks and boards offshore. Check the wind before you paddle out.
